{{Short description|Swedish physicist (born 1950)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2025}}
'''Thors Hans Hansson''' (born 1950) is a Swedish [[physicist]] working as a professor of [[theoretical physics]] at [[Stockholm University]], who was also the head of [[Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics|Nordita]].<ref name="Nordita">{{cite web|
title=Thors Hans Hannson Ny Director För Nordita|
url=https://www.fysik.su.se/blog/thors-hans-hansson-ny-direktor-for-nordita/|
accessdate=4 September 2017|
date=2 February 2016
}}</ref> He is a member of the Nobel Committee for Physics, which each year selects laureates of the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Nobel Committee for Physics|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/prize_awarder/committee.html|accessdate=4 September 2017}}</ref>

==Life==
Hansson received a PhD in 1979 at [[University of Gothenburg]] with a doctorate in [[Elementary particle]] ([[quarks]]). His recent research has been theoretical aspects of [[condensed matter physics]].

He is active in the [[popularization]] of physics and science by including lectures, articles in newspapers and in ''[[Folkvett]]''.

Hansson was elected as a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|title=Newly elected Academy members - from quantum physics to poetry|url=https://www.kva.se/sv/Nyheter/Nyheter2009/Nyinvalda-akademiledamoter---fran-kvantfysik-till-poesi|accessdate=26 October 2011}}</ref> He became director of Nordita in early 2016.<ref name="Nordita"/>

In 2016, on the occasion of the announcement of the 2016 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]], Hansson gave the committee's public explanation of the prize. His use of a cinnamon bun, a bagel, and a pretzel (to explain relevant [[topology|topological ideas]]) was featured in many news reports of the announcement.<ref>{{cite web|title=3 Who Studied Unusual States of Matter Win Nobel Prize in Physics|work=The New York Times |date=4 October 2016 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/10/05/science/nobel-prize-physics-topology.html|accessdate=4 September 2017 |last1=Overbye |first1=Dennis |last2=Chan |first2=Sewell }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bagels, Pretzels and the Nobel Prize in Physics|website=[[Scientific American]] |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/bagels-pretzels-and-the-nobel-prize-in-physics/|accessdate=4 September 2017}}</ref>
